q: For a sequence fₙ in L^p([0,1]) (1 < p < ∞) that is bounded and converges pointwise a.e. to f, weak convergence fₙ ⇀ f in L^p is guaranteed because:
opts: Pointwise a.e. convergence implies strong convergence
Boundedness + pointwise a.e. convergence implies weak convergence (by Dunford-Pettis and reflexivity)
Strong and weak convergence coincide in L^p
Every L^p-bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence by reflexivity, and the limit must be f
exp: L^p for p ∈ (1,∞) is reflexive, so bounded sequences have weakly convergent subsequences. If fₙ → f a.e. and fₙ is bounded in L^p, any weak cluster point must equal f a.e. (by testing against indicators), so fₙ ⇀ f.
